incidents.victim: Multiple organizations worldwide (via Fox Tempest service)
incidents.vector: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, with Europol and FBI support, unsealed legal action and seized infrastructure of Fox Tempest, a malware-signing-as-a-service operation that abused Microsoft Artifact Signing to legitimize malware for ransomware affiliates including Vanilla Tempest (Rhysida), INC, Qilin, and Akira since May 2025.
incidents.impact: Service signed malware delivered via fake Teams, AnyDesk, Putty, and Webex downloads, infecting thousands of machines worldwide and enabling ransomware operations against schools, hospitals, and critical infrastructure including prior attacks attributed to Vanilla Tempest on the British Library and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a previously-undisclosed Huawei enterprise router zero-day with specially crafted packets that put devices into a continuous restart loop; Huawei told POST it had never encountered the attack pattern and had no patch available.
incidents.impact: Denial-of-service attack on July 23, 2025 crashed Luxembourg's entire national telecom network for over three hours, knocking out landline, 4G, and 5G mobile service and leaving hundreds of thousands of residents unable to reach emergency services. Details surfaced May 19, 2026; the flaw has no public CVE and no warning has been issued to other operators.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft and extortion
incidents.vector: TeamPCP (UNC6780) published Shai-Hulud worm source code on GitHub, triggering a wave of typosquat clones; the self-replicating malware fires on package install, harvests GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys, cloud credentials, and database strings, then uses stolen maintainer credentials to push poisoned versions of trusted packages.
incidents.impact: Hundreds of npm packages compromised in the latest 'Mini Shai-Hulud' wave; clones with swapped command-and-control infrastructure are spreading autonomously, install OS-level backdoors that survive package removal, and threaten the implicit trust model of CI/CD pipelines and shared developer dependencies.

incidents.vector: CVE-2026-42897, a cross-site scripting flaw in Exchange Outlook Web Access, lets attackers execute arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser context when a specially crafted email is opened, enabling mailbox takeover, session token theft, and persistent forwarding rules.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation reported with no patch yet available four days after disclosure; affects on-premise Exchange Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Mailbox compromise can enable business email compromise and downstream ransomware operations.

incidents.victim: US gas station fuel storage infrastructure
incidents.vector: Iran-linked actors exploited internet-exposed automatic tank gauge (ATG) systems at US gas stations that lacked password protections, manipulating displayed fuel levels though not the physical fuel quantities.
incidents.impact: No service disruption reported, but the breaches expand Iran's cyber pressure campaign against US infrastructure during the active US/Israel-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz crisis, demonstrating Iranian ability to reach into community-level US systems for strategic signaling.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft and extortion
incidents.vector: Storm-2949 abused Microsoft's Self-Service Password Reset and social-engineered users (including IT staff and senior leadership) into approving fraudulent MFA prompts, then registered attacker-controlled authenticators, locked out victims, and pivoted from Microsoft 365 (OneDrive, SharePoint) into Azure App Services, Key Vaults, storage accounts, and SQL databases using legitimate cloud management features.
incidents.impact: Full identity-driven cloud-wide breach with bulk exfiltration from OneDrive and SharePoint (thousands of files in single downloads) and exploration of production Azure subscriptions; persistence attempts via service-principal credential injection failed only due to insufficient permissions.

incidents.vector: CoinbaseCartel — an offshoot of the Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters collective — obtained a token granting access to Grafana Labs' GitHub environment and downloaded the company's codebase.
incidents.impact: Codebase stolen; Grafana refused to pay ransom citing FBI guidance and stated no customer data, personal information, or customer-system operations were affected. Compromised credentials have been invalidated; the extortion group has attempted to extort 100+ companies since September 2025.

incidents.victim: CISA (US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor maintained a public GitHub repository ('Private-CISA') containing plaintext credentials for multiple highly privileged AWS GovCloud accounts and CISA's internal artifactory code repository; the contractor had disabled GitHub's default secret-scanning protections.
incidents.impact: GitGuardian researchers flagged the exposure as one of the most severe US government data leaks in recent memory, revealing how CISA builds, tests, and deploys internal software. Repository has been taken down but it is unclear whether the credentials were accessed by malicious parties before remediation.

incidents.victim: 13 countries across Middle East and North Africa
incidents.vector: Coordinated Interpol-led law enforcement effort (Operation Ramz) targeting phishing services, scam platforms, malware, and fraud operations across the MENA region.
incidents.impact: 201 arrests, 53 servers seized, 382 suspects identified, and approximately 4,000 victims linked to the operations; police in Jordan also discovered 15 financial-fraud scam operators who were themselves victims of human trafficking. First large-scale MENA cybercrime sweep of its kind.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations in US, UK, Australia
incidents.vector: UNC6671 ('BlackFile') voice-phishes employees on personal phones posing as IT help desk, drives them to lookalike single sign-on portals (.passkeyms[.]com, .enrollms[.]com, .setupsso[.]com), captures credentials and MFA codes in real time via adversary-in-the-middle, registers their own MFA device, then uses Python and PowerShell scripts to mass-exfiltrate from SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce, and Zendesk via Microsoft Graph.
incidents.impact: Ongoing high-cadence extortion campaign active since early 2026 against M365 and Okta tenants; in one incident the actor scripted access to over a million SharePoint and OneDrive files. Extortion escalates to mass-email bombing, executive voicemail threats, and swatting when victims do not engage.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager that gives an unauthenticated remote attacker administrative privileges; Talos tracks the activity as UAT-8616 and has observed infrastructure overlap with Operational Relay Box (ORB) networks.
incidents.impact: Limited but active exploitation observed; additional distinct threat actors are exploiting an older set of Cisco SD-WAN CVEs (CVE-2026-20133, -20128, -20122) in new ways using publicly available proof-of-concept code and JSP webshells. Successful exploitation gives administrative control over a customer's SD-WAN fabric.

incidents.vector: Compromised WordPress sites targeting Australian audiences serve ClickFix-style social-engineering lures that trick users into pasting attacker-supplied commands into Windows Run, which downloads and runs the Vidar information stealer.
incidents.impact: Vidar harvests browser credentials, session cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, and other sensitive data; ACSC issued an alert as part of broader warnings about ongoing targeting of online code repositories and credential-theft campaigns against Australian users.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: Likely state-sponsored cluster CL-STA-1132 exploited zero-day CVE-2026-0300, a buffer overflow in the PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal (Captive Portal), to gain unauthenticated root code execution by injecting shellcode into an nginx worker process; post-exploitation deployed open-source EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunnels, enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account credentials, and methodically wiped crash dumps and audit logs.
incidents.impact: Limited but successful exploitation of internet-exposed firewalls beginning April 9, 2026. Attackers used SAML floods to fail over to a second device and continue access, consistent with the long-running pattern of state-nexus actors targeting edge devices for long-dwell espionage with minimal detection.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and Southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: UAT-8302 deploys custom malware families including 'NetDraft' (a C# variant of FinalDraft/SquidDoor), an updated CloudSorcerer backdoor previously used against Russian government targets, VSHELL with SNOWLIGHT, and a new Rust-based 'SNOWRUST' stager to establish persistent footholds in compromised government networks.
incidents.impact: Long-running China-nexus campaign targeting government agencies in South America since late 2024 and southeastern Europe through 2025; tooling overlap links the group to multiple previously-disclosed Chinese threat clusters and indicates close cooperation among Chinese espionage operations.
